Apple Cranberry Muffins

These apple cranberry muffins are moist, tender and packed with cozy fall flavor - sweet chunks of apple, tart pops of cranberry and warm cinnamon in every bite. A quick high-heat start gives them tall, domed bakery-style tops. They come together in one bowl and are perfect for breakfast, snacking or a grab-and-go treat.

I can't get enough muffins, from cranberry orange muffins to cinnamon streusel muffins to pumpkin banana muffins.

But the apple-and-cranberry combo might be my favorite fall pairing: the apple keeps them moist and adds sweetness while the cranberries bring a tart bite that keeps them from being one-note. A little orange zest and sour cream in the batter make them extra tender and bakery-style. If you love baking with apples this time of year, they're right at home next to my apple cider donuts and apple custard pie.

Why You Will Love These Apple Cranberry Muffins

  • Moist and tender - Sour cream, butter and fresh apple keep the crumb soft and moist for days, not dry and crumbly.
  • Sweet-tart fall flavor - Sweet apple and warm cinnamon against tart cranberries is the perfect autumn balance, brightened with a little orange zest.
  • Bakery-style domed tops - Starting the bake at a high 425°F before dropping the heat gives that tall, rounded muffin-top rise you get from a bakery.

How Do You Get Tall, Bakery-Style Muffin Tops?

The secret to tall, domed muffin tops is a blast of high heat at the start. Baking at 425°F for the first 5 minutes gives the batter a rapid burst of rise before the baking soda and powder settle, pushing the tops up into a dome; then you drop the heat to 350°F to bake through gently without burning.

Two other things matter just as much: don't overmix the batter, and fill the muffin cups all the way to the top. Overmixing develops gluten and makes muffins dense and tough, so you fold the batter just until the flour disappears. And filling the cups full gives the batter enough volume to rise up and over the edge like a bakery muffin.

Ingredient Notes

Full list is in the card; these five carry the muffins.

  • Apples - Peeled and diced into ½-inch chunks so you get soft bites of apple throughout. A firm, sweet-tart variety like Honeycrisp, Fuji or Granny Smith holds its shape best and won't turn to mush.
  • Cranberries - Fresh or frozen (no need to thaw). They add tart, jammy pops that cut the sweetness. If your only option is dried, use ⅓ cup and expect a sweeter, chewier result.
  • Sour cream - The tenderizer. Its fat and acidity make the crumb rich and moist and give a subtle tang. Full-fat is best; Greek yogurt works as a swap.
  • Orange zest - A small but mighty addition. It brightens the whole muffin and pairs naturally with cranberry - the same trick that makes cranberry orange muffins work.
  • Butter and two sugars - Creamed butter with granulated plus a little brown sugar gives richness and a soft, moist crumb with a hint of caramel depth.

Ingredient Swaps

Make them your own:

  • Apples → firm pears for a softer, sweeter bite.
  • Cranberries → fresh or frozen blueberries, or dried cranberries (use less).
  • Sour cream → full-fat Greek yogurt or buttermilk.
  • Add-ins - ½ cup chopped toasted pecans or walnuts for crunch, or a cinnamon-sugar streusel top.
  • Make it healthier - swap half the all-purpose flour for whole wheat, like I do in my morning glory muffins.

How to Make Apple Cranberry Muffins

Please note full ingredient list and instructions can be found in recipe card below.

Step 1: Preheat the oven to 425°F and line or grease a 12-count muffin pan. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.

Step 2: Cream the butter and sugars 2-3 minutes, then beat in the eggs, sour cream, orange zest and vanilla until uniform.

Step 3: With the mixer on low, add the dry ingredients and milk and mix just until combined.

Step 4: Fold in the apples and cranberries by hand.

Tip: Stop mixing the moment the flour disappears, and fold the fruit in by hand. Overmixing is the number-one muffin mistake. It develops gluten and makes them dense and tough instead of light. A few lumps in the batter are exactly what you want.

Step 5: Spoon the batter into the cups, filling them all the way to the top, and sprinkle with raw sugar.

Step 6: Bake 5 minutes at 425°F, then reduce to 350°F (without opening the oven) and bake 15-18 minutes more, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then move to a wire rack.

Tip: Fill the cups to the very top and don't skip the high-heat start. The full cups plus the 425°F blast for the first 5 minutes are what give you tall, domed bakery tops instead of flat ones. The raw sugar on top adds a bakery-style sparkle and crunch.

Apple Cranberry Muffin FAQs

Can I use frozen cranberries?

Yes, and there's no need to thaw them. Add them frozen straight into the batter. Thawed cranberries bleed more color into the batter, so frozen actually keeps the muffins looking cleaner. Add a minute or two to the bake if needed.

What apples are best for muffins

Firm, sweet-tart apples like Honeycrisp, Fuji, Braeburn or Granny Smith. They hold their shape and don't turn watery or mushy the way softer apples can. Dice them small so they cook through.

Why are my muffins dense or flat?

Almost always overmixing. Stir the batter just until the flour disappears and fold the fruit in by hand. Also make sure your baking powder and soda are fresh, and don't skip the high-heat start for the rise.

Can I make these into a loaf?

Yes. Pour the batter into a greased 9x5 loaf pan and bake at 350°F for 55-60 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. Let it cool 10 minutes before removing from the pan.

How do I store apple cranberry muffins?

Keep them airtight at room temperature for 3 days or in the fridge for a week. They freeze well for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or warm briefly in the microwave.

Pro Tips/Recipe Notes

  • Room-temperature ingredients - Eggs, sour cream and butter at room temperature blend into a smooth, even batter.
  • Don't overmix - Fold just until combined; it's the difference between tender and tough.
  • Fill the cups full - All the way to the top for tall, domed bakery-style muffins.
  • High heat first - The 425°F start sets the dome before you drop to 350°F to bake through.
  • Toss fruit in a little flour - Optional, but tossing the apples and cranberries in a teaspoon of flour helps keep them from sinking to the bottom.

Apple Cranberry Muffins

Ryan Beck
These apple cranberry muffins are moist, tender and full of fall flavor - sweet apple, tart cranberries and warm cinnamon with bakery-style domed tops.
5 from 2 votes
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prevent your screen from going dark
Prep Time 10 minutes mins
Cook Time 20 minutes mins
Total Time 30 minutes mins
Course Breakfast
Cuisine American
Servings 12 muffins
Calories 232 kcal

Ingredients
  

  • 1 ¾ cups all-purpose flour (219g)
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • ½ cup unsalted butter at room temperature
  • ½ cup granulated sugar
  • ¼ cup light brown sugar
  • 2 large eggs at room temperature
  • ½ cup sour cream at room temperature
  • 1 tablespoon orange zest
  • 2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • ¼ cup whole milk
  • 1 cup apples peeled and diced into ½ inch chunks
  • ½ cup cranberries fresh or frozen
  • 1 tablespoon raw sugar for topping

Instructions
 

  • Preheat oven to 425 °F (218 °C). Spray a 12-count muffin pan with nonstick spray or line with cupcake liners. Set aside.
  • Mix together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl and set aside.
    1 ¾ cups all-purpose flour , 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, ½ teaspoon salt
  • In bowl of mixer, cream together the butter and sugars until combined, about 2-3 minutes. Add in the eggs, sour cream, orange zest and vanilla extract and beat on medium speed until the texture is uniform.
    ½ cup unsalted butter, ½ cup granulated sugar, ¼ cup light brown sugar, 2 large eggs, ½ cup sour cream, 1 tablespoon orange zest, 2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • With mixer running on low speed, add the dry ingredients and milk and mix until combined. Fold in the apples and cranberries.
    ¼ cup whole milk, 1 cup apples, ½ cup cranberries
  • Spoon batter into prepared muffin pan, filling them all the way to the top. Sprinkle some sugar over top.
    1 tablespoon raw sugar
  • Bake for 5 minutes at 425 °F (218 °C) and then reduce heat to 350 °F (177 °C). Continue to bake for 15-18 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Allow muffins to cool for 5 minutes in pan before transferring to a wire rack to cool.

Notes

  • Use room-temperature eggs, sour cream and butter.
  • Mix just until combined; fold fruit by hand.
  • Fill cups to the top for domed muffins.
  • Start at 425°F, then drop to 350°F.
  • Dice apples ½ inch so they cook through.
